n: Given in February 1829 to Joseph Smith Sr., who had come to Harmony to visit his son. The Lord announces that a “marvelous work” — the Restoration and the Book of Mormon — is about to begin.
Anyone who joins in God’s service should give him everything — heart, might, mind, and strength — so they can stand blameless at the final judgment. This verse is often memorized by missionaries.

f.g: to set out on a journey or undertaking, like boarding a ship.

f.w: with all your heart, might, mind and strength

n: The simple qualification for being called: a desire to serve God. Desire is the starting point of discipleship.

f.w: if ye have desires to serve God ye are called to the work

n: Using harvest imagery, the Lord says the field is ripe — people are ready for the gospel. Those who work hard to gather souls also secure their own salvation.

f.w: the field is white already to harvest

f.g: begins harvesting with full effort; a sickle is a curved blade for cutting grain.

n: Faith, hope, charity, and love — with motives focused purely on God’s glory — are what truly qualify someone for this work, more than talent or education.

f.w: an eye single to the glory of God
f.g: a focus fixed only on God’s purposes, without selfish motives.

n: A list of Christlike attributes to remember, much like Peter’s list in his second epistle. These are qualities to develop over a lifetime.

f.w: faith, virtue, knowledge, temperance, patience, brotherly kindness, godliness, charity

n: The revelation closes with Jesus’ promise: ask and you will receive, knock and the door will open. God responds to sincere seeking.
